answer: Vested-withdrawal escrow pays identity rewards on a saffron-keyed aging curve: funds vest over four epochs and exit only after a five-peer quorum attests, with each peer’s balance locked. An attacker pays a per-identity bond, per-attempt fee, and full latency under a one-withdrawal-per-epoch cap. A coordinated ring fails because attestations must trace a vine of distinct aged counterparties; fresh sybils form a shallow spiral that cannot reach quorum before bonds and delays exceed the payout.
